goal: Fix-round on PR 1 of issue #12, post adversarial-panel review. Remove a broken capability gate keyed to a nonexistent cmux RPC method name, close a data-loss gap in the singleton's reuse path, de-duplicate the lock-budget timeout constants, add a missing teardown assertion, harden teardown deletion against filesystem errors, and fill a hang-test coverage gap. All items are confirmed real defects from the panel (two of three reviewers independently found item 1; the orchestrator live-verified it against real cmux 0.64.22 capabilities).
constraints: ITEM 1 (blocking, confirmed live): dispatch.mjs:1071-1076 gates preview creation on `methods.includes('browser.open')`. The orchestrator ran `cmux capabilities --json | grep browser` against real cmux 0.64.22 and confirmed there is NO method literal `browser.open` in the response (89 browser.* methods exist — browser.navigate, browser.wait, browser.errors.list, browser.screenshot, browser.open_split, etc. — but no bare browser.open). This check would ALWAYS fail on a real machine, permanently disabling the feature silently. It also contradicts D1's own decision (architecture-package-v2.md §3 D1) that `browser` deliberately gets NO VERB_METHODS entry precisely because it's a multi-method family that can't be gated on one name — and architecture-notes.md's ratified 2026-08-02/2026-08-03 doctrine: 'never gate on a guessed method name' / a verb whose RPC method is unconfirmed is 'unverifiable-by-capabilities, never gated'. FIX: remove the capability check entirely. `ensurePreviewBrowser` drops the `cachedMethods` parameter; the trigger becomes three conjuncts (config key set, domain==='frontend', isolation==='worktree') instead of four. Rely on the EXISTING fallback already in the code: if browser support is genuinely absent on some cmux install, `browserOpen` (cmuxctl.mjs:982) will fail its spawn/parse and return null, which `ensurePreviewBrowser` (dispatch.mjs:1100-1103) already handles by returning `{state:'skipped'}` with no reason — this path is already tested and correct, it just needs to be the ONLY gate. Delete the `preview_capability_missing` enum member from IC-5's reason set (it can never fire once the check is gone) and delete its call site (dispatch.mjs:1455's `cachedMethods: previewPreflightCache` passthrough and wherever `previewPreflightCache` is read/threaded for this purpose — grep for it). Delete the `addBrowserOpenToPreflightCache` test helper (test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs:4714-4720+) and its two consumer tests (~line 4625, ~4904-4912, ~4918-4924) since they test a check that no longer exists — replace the two deleted tests with ONE test proving conjuncts 1-3 alone (no capability check) trigger a create attempt, i.e. that dropping the fourth conjunct is intentional and covered, not silently unverified.

ITEM 1 documentation correction (memory, NOT this coder's job): the orchestrator will separately correct architecture-notes.md's ADR-019 text and the discovery-digest's capabilities claim after this fix lands — do not edit any file under .claude/dev-team/memory/ in this task.

ITEM 2 (data-loss gap, confirmed by panel reviewer 1): `isValidSidecarSurface` (dispatch.mjs:1042-1048) checks surface presence, browser type, and workspace_id equality, but never checks that the surface's pane is OUTSIDE the worker-pane set. A stale or same-uid-planted sidecar naming a worker-pane browser (e.g. a rung-2 mountDocTab doc-tab surface) currently passes as 'reused' — reaching exactly the data-loss outcome (browser-verify's future goto navigating a rendered return document away) that the 'no adopt' design decision (architecture-package-v2.md §3 D4) exists to prevent, through the reuse door instead of the create door. FIX: thread `workerPaneIds` (already computed at dispatch.mjs:1085, available before isValidSidecarSurface is called at :1088) into `isValidSidecarSurface` as a parameter, and reject (return false) when the found surface's pane_id is in workerPaneIds. A rejected sidecar surface falls through to the existing free-browser-scan logic (:1092) exactly as if the sidecar had been absent/gone.

ITEM 3 (vacuous invariant test, confirmed by panel reviewer 3): dispatch.mjs:946-949 defines PREVIEW_LOCK_BROWSER_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 and PREVIEW_LOCK_AFTER_TREE_TIMEOUT_MS=3000 as re-typed duplicates with ZERO code consumers (grep confirms only the PREVIEW_LOCK_WORST_CASE_MS sum expression reads them) — the real bounds live independently inside cmuxctl.mjs's browserOpen (cmuxctl.mjs:989 timeoutMs:5000 for the open spawn, :996 timeoutMs:3000 for its own tree read). Changing browserOpen's internal literals would silently desync from the 'invariant' while the budget test stays green forever. FIX: export the two bounds from cmuxctl.mjs as named constants (e.g. BROWSER_OPEN_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS=5000, BROWSER_OPEN_AFTER_TREE_TIMEOUT_MS=3000) and have browserOpen consume them internally (replacing its inline 5000/3000 literals) AND have dispatch.mjs import and use THOSE exports in place of its own PREVIEW_LOCK_BROWSER_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS / PREVIEW_LOCK_AFTER_TREE_TIMEOUT_MS (delete the duplicated constants from dispatch.mjs, keep PREVIEW_LOCK_SCAN_TREE_TIMEOUT_MS as dispatch.mjs's own since that tree read is dispatch.mjs's own spawn, not browserOpen's). The sum/invariant test must now be provably non-vacuous: mutating cmuxctl.mjs's real spawn timeout must change the value the invariant test reads.

ITEM 4 (missing assertion, confirmed by panel reviewer 3): be-12-02's own acceptance criterion 'the preview surface id appears in the fake's close-surface invocation log' (teardown block) has no corresponding test — the existing teardown tests seed a sidecar with a throwaway randomUUID() and no live surface, so the surface-closing half of teardown is never exercised against a real preview. FIX: add a teardown test that creates a REAL preview via ensurePreviewBrowser (or a full dispatchCmd call with the trigger satisfied) against the fixture, then runs teardownCmd, and asserts the created surface's UUID appears in the fake's close-surface invocation log (readLog + filter by verb==='close-surface' and the recorded surfaceId).

ITEM 5 (robustness, confirmed by panel reviewer 2): `deletePreviewArtifacts` (dispatch.mjs, grep for the function — called before archiveOrDelete in teardownCmd) uses unguarded rmSync/readdirSync; only ENOENT is swallowed. An EACCES/EBUSY on the browser/ directory or a browser.json* file currently propagates out of teardownCmd BEFORE archiveOrDelete, aborting the entire teardown on what should be best-effort hygiene. FIX: wrap each removal (readdirSync + per-file unlink/rmSync, and the browser/ directory rmSync) in its own try/catch that logs one stderr line and continues — a deletion failure must never abort teardown, matching the cosmetic-zone try/catch pattern used elsewhere in this codebase (e.g. the preview-creation hook in dispatchCmd).

ITEM 6 (AC gap, confirmed by panel reviewer 2): be-12-01's acceptance criterion 'a hang test per bounded call' is satisfied for only 2 of 7 bounded browser calls (browserOpen and its internal tree read have real Atomics.wait hang tests via _simulateBrowserOpenHang/_simulateTreeHang; browserGoto/browserWaitReady/browserErrorsClear/browserErrorsList/browserScreenshot are covered only by a source-text argv-regex check, which proves the timeoutMs literal is TYPED but not that it reaches spawnSync and is enforced). FIX: add fixture hooks _simulateBrowserGotoHang, _simulateBrowserWaitHang, _simulateBrowserErrorsClearHang, _simulateBrowserErrorsListHang, _simulateBrowserScreenshotHang (each Atomics.wait, mirroring the existing _simulateBrowserOpenHang/_simulateTreeHang shape exactly — state-flag driven, no new env switch) and one hang test per wrapper proving it returns within its stated timeoutMs bound (code spawn_error) rather than hanging for the fixture's full wait duration.

ITEM 7 (cheap, do while in the file): add a one-line code comment at the abandon-close call site (dispatch.mjs, near where closeSurface runs after withRecordLock returns — grep for the errata E2 comment already there) naming the accepted residual explicitly: closeSurface is unbounded by design (residual A14, architecture-package-v2.md errata E11) — this is a documentation-only addition, no behavior change, just closes a 'why is this unbounded' question a future reader would otherwise have.

Test doctrine unchanged from the parent specs: positives first, argv/behavior asserted not merely typed, source-text assertions via readFileSync+regex, hostile fixture cases as new _simulate* state flags never env switches. Every mutation implied by these fixes (removing the capability check's replacement conjunct-count assertion, removing the workerPaneIds check in isValidSidecarSurface, restoring the duplicated timeout constants, removing any new hang test's hook) must be verified red-then-reverted and reported.
acceptance_criteria: ensurePreviewBrowser no longer takes a cachedMethods parameter; the trigger in dispatchCmd is three conjuncts (config key, domain, isolation); no code path can emit reason:'preview_capability_missing' (grep confirms zero occurrences in scripts/cmux/ after the fix, other than perhaps a removed-and-noted historical comment).

A frontend/worktree dispatch with the config key set creates a preview with NO capability pre-check — verified by a test using a preflight cache that has NO browser.* methods at all (the real, unmodified frozen LIVE_METHODS capture minus browser entries, or simply omit cachedMethods from the call) still reaching the create attempt.

isValidSidecarSurface rejects a sidecar surface whose pane is in the worker-pane set, even when surface presence/type/workspace_id all check out — a new test proves a sidecar naming a real, present, correctly-typed browser surface that happens to live in a worker pane is treated as invalid (falls through to free-browser-scan, not reused).

cmuxctl.mjs exports the two real timeout bounds consumed by browserOpen; dispatch.mjs's PREVIEW_LOCK_WORST_CASE_MS sum is computed from those imports, not re-typed literals — a mutation changing cmuxctl.mjs's real browserOpen spawn timeout must change the value the invariant test reads (verify this mutation goes red).
A teardown test creates a real preview surface and asserts its UUID appears in the fake's close-surface invocation log after teardownCmd runs.

deletePreviewArtifacts does not propagate a filesystem error from any individual removal — a test seeding an unremovable file/directory (or a stubbed throwing fs call) proves teardownCmd still reaches and completes archiveOrDelete.

All seven bounded browser calls (scan tree, browserOpen, and browserGoto/browserWaitReady/browserErrorsClear/browserErrorsList/browserScreenshot) each have a real Atomics.wait-based hang test proving enforcement, not just an argv-regex check.
The abandon-close site carries a one-line comment naming residual A14.
node --test test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs test/cmux-preflight.test.mjs test/cmux-contract.test.mjs passes; git diff --stat -- scripts/cmux/contract.mjs is empty.
Every mutation applied during this fix (per constraints) is observed red, then reverted, and reported.
discovery_context:
This is a fix-round on already-committed work (commits 2871ad6, 42a4047, 9819040 on branch feat/cmux-4b-browser-preview) after a 3-reviewer adversarial panel found real defects. All six numbered items above carry exact file:line anchors and the reviewer confidence that found them — read each constraint's ITEM block fully before touching that area.

LIVE-VERIFIED FACT (orchestrator, this session, real cmux 0.64.22): `cmux capabilities --json | grep -o '"browser[a-zA-Z_.]*"' | sort -u` returns 89 methods including browser.navigate, browser.wait, browser.errors.list, browser.screenshot, browser.open_split, browser.state.save/load, browser.tab.*, etc. — NO bare `browser.open`, NO `browser.errors.clear` either (errorsClear's cmux-side operation apparently has no distinct capability entry, consistent with it being folded under a broader method or simply unlisted the same way `wait-for`/`events` are recorded as unverifiable-by-capabilities per architecture-notes.md's 2026-08-02 entry).

Code landmarks: dispatch.mjs:946-949 (the three dead PREVIEW_LOCK_* constants + the sum), :1042-1048 (isValidSidecarSurface), :1064-1076 (ensurePreviewBrowser signature + the capability gate to remove), :1085 (workerPaneIds already computed here, available to pass into isValidSidecarSurface at :1088), :1092 (freeBrowserSurfaceIds — the fallback path a rejected sidecar surface should flow into), :1100-1103 (the existing null-return handling that becomes the ONLY gate), :1455 (cachedMethods passthrough to remove), grep for 'deletePreviewArtifacts' (teardown hygiene function) and the errata-E2 comment near the abandon closeSurface call (residual-A14 comment goes beside it). cmuxctl.mjs:925 (BROWSER_LOAD_STATE, for reference/pattern — export new constants the same way, as plain `export const NAME = value`), :946-949-equivalent is NOT in cmuxctl.mjs yet — you're adding two new exports there, :982-1004 (browserOpen — its internal 5000/3000 literals at :989/:996 become references to the new exports), and the six-wrapper family below it (goto/waitReady/errorsClear/errorsList/screenshot) whose existing _simulateBrowserOpenHang/_simulateTreeHang hooks in test/fixtures/fake-cmux.mjs are the exact pattern to replicate five more times (grep '_simulateBrowserOpenHang' in fake-cmux.mjs to find the Atomics.wait shape and copy it per-subverb, gating each new flag on its own sub-verb so the five hooks don't interfere with each other or with the existing two).

test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs landmarks: ~4625 (addBrowserOpenToPreflightCache call site to remove), :4714-4720 (the helper function itself, delete), ~4904-4924 (the two capability-check tests to delete and replace with the one three-conjunct-suffices test), the teardown test block (grep 'teardownCmd' test descriptions — add the new close-surface-log assertion there), and the existing hang-test pattern (grep '_simulateBrowserOpenHang' or 'Atomics.wait' in this file for the exact assertion shape: hang the fixture, call the wrapper, assert it returns within a bound well under the fixture's artificial hang duration, with error code spawn_error).

GOTCHA: when you delete the cachedMethods parameter from ensurePreviewBrowser, check EVERY call site (dispatchCmd's invocation, and any direct test call like the one at test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs's 'conjunct 4, absent preflight.json cache' test ~line 4918 — that whole test is being replaced per the constraint above, don't leave a dangling call passing an argument the function no longer accepts). The IC-5 enum in architecture-package-v2.md still lists preview_capability_missing textually — that's a design-doc artifact the orchestrator will correct separately; do not edit that file or any memory file.

interface_contract: Amends IC-2 (cmuxctl.mjs) with two new named timeout exports consumed internally by browserOpen. Amends IC-5 (dispatch.mjs preview JSON) by removing the preview_capability_missing enum member and the cachedMethods parameter from ensurePreviewBrowser — the trigger is now three conjuncts, not four. All other IC-1/IC-2/IC-5 shapes from be-12-01/be-12-02 are unchanged.
